pages.text: Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) right guidance, and He knew that he was worthy of it. And Ibrahim was calling people to this guidance.

His father and his people worshipped idols that they had made, and kept to their worship. He said to them: ﴿مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'What are these statues to which you keep devoted?' And they worshipped them following their forefathers.

When his people had gone away, Ibrahim broke the idols into small pieces, and left the biggest of them so that they would come back to it and ask it. When they came back and saw their idols broken, they brought Ibrahim before the eyes of the people.

They turned to themselves and their error became clear to them, but soon they went back to their stubbornness. Ibrahim said to them: ﴿أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـٔٗا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'Do you then worship, instead of Allah, what can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?' When their argument had failed, they lit a huge fire to burn him with it, and threw him into it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدٗا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'We said: O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim.' And no harm reached him in it, and nothing bad befell him.

His people wanted to destroy him, but Allah made their plot come to nothing and made them the losers. Among the lessons of these verses: idols can neither benefit nor harm, so none is worshipped but Allah. Another is that Allah gave victory to His messenger Ibrahim, and made the fire coolness and safety for him.
